sŏphĭa  (i long,
				Prud. Sym. 122;
			id. Cath. 1613;
			Fortun. Suppl. 2, 62),
		ae, f., = σοφία, 
I.wisdom (pure Lat. sapientia): sophiam, sapientia quae
			perhibetur, Enn. ap. Fest. p. 325 Müll. (Ann.
			v. 227 Vahl.); Afran. ap. Gell. 13, 8, 3; Mart. 1,
				112, 1; cf. Sen. Ep. 89, 6;
				Lact. 3, 16, 10 (in Cic. Off.
				1, 43, 153, written as Greek).
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
